newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RODRIGUEZ RESIGNS WITH RANGERS FOR $42 MLN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RODRIGUEZ RESIGNS WITH RANGERS FOR $42 MLN.

text.p: The Texas Rangers re-signed All-Star catcher Ivan Rodriguez to a five-year, $42 million contract on Thursday.

Rodriguez, who joined the Rangers in 1991, will get a $1 million signing bonus on the new contract and will be paid $6 million next year, $8 million a year for the next three years and $9 million in 2002.
He also gets a $2 million severance bonus if he ever leaves the club.

"I'm very happy to stay another five years with the Rangers," Rodriguez, 25, told a news conference at the Rangers' ballpark in Arlington, Texas. "This is the team I want to be with for the rest of my career."
Rodriguez, who was born in Puerto Rico, has won five consecutive American League Gold Glove Awards and is a six-time All-Star catcher.
He turned down a Rangers contract offer last week that would have guaranteed him $38.2 million for the next five years. He said he wanted at least $45 million.
The Rangers said that was their final offer and appeared ready to trade him before Thursday's trading deadline rather than risk losing him to free agency at the end of the season.
The club earlier this week traded starting pitcher Ken Hill to the Anaheim Angels in exchange for catcher Jim Leyritz to limit the damage of Rodriguez' possible departure.
But the Rangers received no lucrative trade offers for Rodriguez and continued negotiations with the young star.

Rodriguez played a key role as the Rangers won the American League West title last year and has been one of its most consistent players this year even as the team has struggled, hitting a .332 average with 11 home runs and 47 RBIs.
"Ivan has been with us since he was a very young man. He has grown to be a star with us and we want him to be a Hall of Famer," Rangers president Tom Schieffer said.
